functions.name: After
functions.summary: After waits for the duration to elapse and then sends the current time on the returned channel. It is equivalent to [NewTimer](d).C.

functions.name: AfterFunc
functions.summary: AfterFunc waits for the duration to elapse and then calls f in its own goroutine. It returns a [Timer] that can be used to cancel the call using its Stop method. The returned Timer's C field is not used and will be nil.

functions.name: FixedZone
functions.summary: FixedZone returns a [Location] that always uses the given zone name and offset (seconds east of UTC).

functions.name: LoadLocation
functions.summary: LoadLocation returns the Location with the given name.

functions.name: LoadLocationFromTZData
functions.summary: LoadLocationFromTZData returns a Location with the given name initialized from the IANA Time Zone database-formatted data. The data should be in the format of a standard IANA time zone file (for example, the content of /etc/localtime on Unix systems).

functions.name: NewTicker
functions.summary: NewTicker returns a new [Ticker] containing a channel that will send the current time on the channel after each tick. The period of the ticks is specified by the duration argument. The ticker will adjust the time interval or drop ticks to make up for slow receivers. The duration d must be greater than zero; if not, NewTicker will panic.

functions.name: NewTimer
functions.summary: NewTimer creates a new Timer that will send the current time on its channel after at least duration d.

functions.name: Now
functions.summary: Now returns the current local time.

functions.name: Parse
functions.summary: Parse parses a formatted string and returns the time value it represents. See the documentation for the constant called [Layout] to see how to represent the format. The second argument must be parseable using the format string (layout) provided as the first argument.

lines: pkg time, func Parse(string, string) (Time, error)

functions.name: ParseDuration
functions.summary: ParseDuration parses a duration string. A duration string is a possibly signed sequence of decimal numbers, each with optional fraction and a unit suffix, such as "300ms", "-1.5h" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "ns", "us" (or "µs"), "ms", "s", "m", "h".

functions.name: ParseInLocation
functions.summary: ParseInLocation is like Parse but differs in two important ways. First, in the absence of time zone information, Parse interprets a time as UTC; ParseInLocation interprets the time as in the given location. Second, when given a zone offset or abbreviation, Parse tries to match it against the Local location; ParseInLocation uses the given location.

functions.name: Since
functions.summary: Since returns the time elapsed since t. It is shorthand for time.Now().Sub(t).

functions.name: Sleep
functions.summary: Sleep pauses the current goroutine for at least the duration d. A negative or zero duration causes Sleep to return immediately.

functions.name: Tick
functions.summary: Tick is a convenience wrapper for [NewTicker] providing access to the ticking channel only. Unlike NewTicker, Tick will return nil if d <= 0.

functions.name: Unix
functions.summary: Unix returns the local Time corresponding to the given Unix time, sec seconds and nsec nanoseconds since January 1, 1970 UTC. It is valid to pass nsec outside the range [0, 999999999]. Not all sec values have a corresponding time value. One such value is 1<<63-1 (the largest int64 value).

functions.name: UnixMicro
functions.summary: UnixMicro returns the local Time corresponding to the given Unix time, usec microseconds since January 1, 1970 UTC.

functions.name: UnixMilli
functions.summary: UnixMilli returns the local Time corresponding to the given Unix time, msec milliseconds since January 1, 1970 UTC.

functions.name: Until
functions.summary: Until returns the duration until t. It is shorthand for t.Sub(time.Now()).
